claim_verdicts.suggested_text: While the first future is waiting (no initialData, no earlier future completed) or after a future fails, snapshot.data is null. When a new future replaces one that completed, the waiting snapshot keeps the previous result.

issues.text: True for the first load only. §5 now says the Future is 'replaced ... when the user refreshes' (line 27 _reload); FutureBuilder docs: in waiting 'unless a future has previously completed ... the previous result persists'. On refresh the waiting snapshot holds the old list (or old error), so 'while waiting there is no data' is false there. Round-2 issues (unlisted claim -> claim 9, 'yet' removed; 'once' -> 'first Future', summary line 4) are resolved.
issues.quote: while the `Future` is waiting or has failed there is no data
issues.fix: Write 'while the first `Future` is still waiting, or after it has failed, there is no data'. Update claim 9 text to the suggested_text in claim_verdicts n=9.

issues.text: Round-1 order gap is fixed. New small snag: 'the first Future' makes me ask what a second one is and what the snapshot holds while it waits. §4 has not yet said the Future can be replaced; that only comes in §5 ('when the user refreshes'), and the lesson never says what a refresh shows while waiting.
issues.quote: while the first `Future` is still waiting, or after it has failed, there is no data
issues.fix: Add a few words after 'the first `Future`', e.g. '(the screen can later swap in a new one when the user refreshes; see below)', so the word 'first' is not a puzzle at this point.

issues.text: Still true from round 1: in q1, q4 and q5 the correct option is the longest and most specific, so I could pick it by length alone (q2 is now close to its wrong options).
issues.quote: So each rebuild reuses the same request instead of starting a new one
issues.fix: In q1, q4 and q5, make one or two wrong options as long and specific as the correct one, or shorten the correct one.

issues.text: Unchanged from round 1: the statement repeats the first 'Beginners often think' item almost word for word, so memory of that section is enough to mark it false.
issues.quote: Statement: an empty product list and a still-loading one can show the same blank screen, since the user can't tell the difference anyway.
issues.fix: Rephrase the statement as a small situation, e.g. a developer proposes showing nothing until the products arrive, and ask whether that is fine.

issues.text: The correct explanation is now clear ('mapping' is gone). The wrong-option explanations b/c/d still use 'would matter only when ... were', which I had to re-read to find the plain reason.
issues.quote: A bug like that would matter only when every successful load showed an error, but the screen normally shows the list.
issues.fix: Rewrite b/c/d plainly, e.g. b: 'If FutureBuilder did that, every successful load would show an error, but the screen normally shows the list.'
